points.t: Mild–moderate acne in a young adult, or a woman who also wants **contraception** or has **hormonal** acne.
Sebum, follicular plugging, *C. acnes* and inflammation; androgens drive sebum, so **oestrogen-containing pills help**.
**Fixed topical combination for 12 weeks**; add oral tetracycline for moderate–severe (never alone); COC as an option.
**VTE** with COCs, especially co-cyprindiol (UKMEC); mood change; scarring acne needing isotretinoin.

cause.lead: Four mechanisms, and drugs that hit each one.
points: **Androgen-driven sebum** → hormonal therapy (COC, spironolactone, co-cyprindiol).
**Follicular hyperkeratinisation** (microcomedone) → topical retinoids, azelaic acid.
*Cutibacterium acnes* → **BPO** (no resistance), antibiotics (resistance).
**Inflammation** → retinoids, azelaic acid, antibiotics. Isotretinoin hits all four.
COC: oestrogen ↑ **SHBG** and suppresses ovarian androgen; anti-androgenic progestogens add blockade.

visuals.caption: From microcomedone to inflamed papule: each acne drug acts at one or more of these steps.

features.lead: Grade it NICE’s way, then pick a 12-week combination.
points: **Mild–moderate**: any comedones, **≤ 34 inflammatory lesions, ≤ 2 nodules**.
**Moderate–severe**: **≥ 35 inflammatory lesions and/or ≥ 3 nodules**; psychological impact can raise the grade.
Lower-face / jawline pattern suggests a hormonal component: ask about hirsutism, weight, cycles.
Worked case: 19-year-old, comedones and pustules on cheeks, jaw, perioral → mild–moderate.

visuals.caption: Hormonal-pattern acne: inflamed papules, pustules and small nodules along the jawline, chin and around the mouth.

points: Adapalene 0.1% + BPO 2.5%; tretinoin 0.025% + clindamycin 1%; or BPO 3–5% + clindamycin 1%.
Adapalene 0.3% + BPO 2.5%; tretinoin + clindamycin; adapalene/BPO **+ oral lymecycline or doxycycline**; or azelaic acid 15–20% + oral tetracycline.
No antibiotic monotherapy; **no topical + oral antibiotic** together; oral only with retinoid or BPO; review at 12 weeks.
**UKMEC**: BMI (≥ 35 = UKMEC 3), BP, **migraine with aura (UKMEC 4)**, VTE history, thrombophilia, postpartum.

cards.name: Tetracyclines
cards.clue: Avoid in pregnancy, breastfeeding, under-12s; doxycycline photosensitivity.

cards.name: Minocycline
cards.clue: Not recommended: lupus-like syndrome, hepatitis, pigmentation.

cards.name: Co-cyprindiol
cards.clue: Not first-line; highest VTE risk; stop plan (review at 3 months).

cards.name: Drospirenone COC
cards.clue: Anti-androgenic; check potassium with ACE-i / ARB / spironolactone.

cards.name: Spironolactone
cards.clue: Off-label, 50–100 mg daily for persistent lower-face acne in women; per formulary.

manage.lead: Skin care, a 12-week combination, then maintain.

points: Non-comedogenic products, gentle cleanser twice daily, no picking, oil-free sunscreen.
No strong evidence for elimination diets (NICE).
Thin layer to the **whole area**, not just spots; irritated → alternate nights or wash off after 1 h.

rx.note: With a topical retinoid or BPO; never with a topical antibiotic.

points: Consider a COC **in addition to topicals** (NICE); choose with UKMEC.
Still a problem after 6 months: third-generation or drospirenone pill; co-cyprindiol for moderate–severe with explicit VTE counselling and stop date.
Clear → stop antibiotic, **maintain** with retinoid ± BPO.
Not improved → switch option; failed two courses incl. oral antibiotic → **refer for isotretinoin**.

visuals.caption: A pea-sized amount dotted on forehead, cheeks, nose and chin, then spread thinly over the whole face, avoiding eyes and lips.
visuals.alt: Pea-sized gel on fingertip and dotted on a face

limits.t: Screen mood and self-harm at every review.

items.t: **Acne fulminans** (fever, arthralgia, ulcerating acne): seen by dermatology **within 24 hours**.
Calf swelling, chest pain or breathlessness on a COC: possible **VTE**.
Scarring, nodulocystic, rapidly worsening acne or severe distress: refer for isotretinoin.

pearls.t: ‘Twelve weeks before judging’: show a calendar.
Retinoids dry and sun-sensitise; BPO bleaches fabrics.
Doxycycline: upright with water; keep antacids and iron 2–3 h apart.
Teach VTE and stroke warning symptoms on a COC.

quiz.q: Can you combine oral and topical antibiotics?
quiz.a: No: oral antibiotics only with a topical retinoid or BPO.

quiz.q: UKMEC category for migraine with aura on a COC?

quiz.a: Moderate–severe acne failing two courses including an oral antibiotic, or scarring / distress.
